chapters.title: Chapter 298: A Billion Dollar Evening
paragraphs: With that, Stan opened his banking app. He structured the transfer as a private equity investment into Maya’s holding company, reviewed the details one final time, and authorized the full $620 million wire transfer in a single transaction.
The confirmation arrived almost immediately.
He mentally logged the expenditure as Maya’s first rebate cycle of the week, one of the four transactions now permitted under System 2.0.
The system responded at once.
[Ding!]
[Investment spending on Maya Zimmerman confirmed.]
[Favorability tier: 120 (12× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $7.44 billion deposited into linked account.]
Stan let out a slow breath. A few seconds later, his banking app refreshed.
An incoming deposit of $7.44 billion appeared under the familiar description:
[Internal Credit Adjustment.]
His account balance had plunged to almost zero the instant the wire transfer left. Now it surged to a figure larger than any amount of liquid cash he had ever possessed. One transaction. One rebate.
His net liquid wealth had increased by $7.44 billion.
He didn’t linger on the number. There was still work to do.
Next, Stan opened TikTuk Live. The discovery feed loaded almost instantly.

Over the past several weeks, the Sir Streak account had trained the platform’s recommendation algorithm well. Rather than random broadcasts, the feed was now populated almost exclusively with top-rated female streamers, creators the algorithm believed matched his viewing and spending habits. The platform was doing anything they
’Perfect.’ He smiled...
He began scrolling. His first target was Kira.
Twenty-three. A former model who had transitioned into livestreaming, she had built a respectable mid-tier audience. The system assigned her a beauty rating of 8.7.
Stan bound her without hesitation.
[Binding successful.]
[Reward: Equity stake acquired in a regional cosmetics company.]
He entered her stream and quietly sent $2 billion worth of gifts. The effect was immediate. The chat descended into chaos.

Kira stared blankly at the rapidly climbing gift counter before covering her mouth with both hands. Seconds later, tears streamed down her face. She repeatedly tried to thank Sir Streak, only to lose her composure each time another wave of gifts appeared.
By the end of the broadcast, the platform had already recorded it as the highest-grossing stream in her channel’s history.
Her favorability settled at 65, genuine gratitude tempered by the lingering disbelief that a complete stranger had just changed her life.
[Favorability tier: 60-69 (6× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $12 billion.]
Stan moved on. The second streamer was Lyra.
[Beauty rating: 8.6.]
She specialized in cooking streams and had cultivated a smaller but unusually loyal community. After binding her, Stan repeated the process. Another $2 billion in gifts.

Lyra froze for several seconds before forcing herself to smile. Years of streaming experience showed through as she regained her composure, thanked Sir Streak with remarkable professionalism, and somehow continued preparing dinner despite the unprecedented flood of donations.
She remained calm.
The excitement in her voice, however, became impossible to hide.
By the end of the stream, her favorability had climbed to 52.
[Favorability tier: 50-59 (5× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $10 billion.]
Without hesitation, Stan opened the next stream. The third target was Sera.
Beauty rating: 8.9.
A high-energy variety streamer whose broadcasts thrived on controlled chaos.
He bound her. Then he spent another $2 billion.
Sera’s reaction was explosive. She screamed. Jumped out of her chair. Paced around the room. Cause what the fuck was that. Returned to the camera. Burst into tears.
Over the next hour, she thanked Sir Streak in three different languages, laughing and crying so often that even her moderators struggled to keep the stream under control.
Her gratitude felt immediate and completely unfiltered.
When the broadcast ended, her favorability had reached 71.
The system quietly highlighted her profile.
[Target demonstrates unusually high emotional responsiveness.]
[Favorability tier: 70-79 (7× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $14 billion.]
Stan acknowledged the notification with a brief glance before moving on. The fourth streamer was Mei.
[Beauty rating: 9.1.]
The system marked her as Exceptional. Stan paid noticeably more attention before completing the bind. Another $2 billion in gifts followed. Unlike the others, Mei never lost control.

A former entertainer, she carried herself with polished professionalism. She expressed sincere appreciation, thanked Sir Streak repeatedly, and maintained the steady composure expected of someone accustomed to performing under pressure.
Even so, the occasional pause and subtle tremor in her voice betrayed just how overwhelming the donations truly were.
Her favorability stabilized at 68. Measured. Sincere. Professional.
[Favorability tier: 60-69 (6× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $12 billion.]
Four new bindings. $8 billion spent. $48 billion returned.
Stan looked at the figures for several moments. Even after weeks of using the system, the scale remained difficult to internalize. Earlier that day, he had considered himself unimaginably wealthy.
Now his account balance was climbing by tens of billions of dollars in a single evening.
Money was beginning to lose its intuitive meaning. It had become numbers. Inputs. Outputs.
A resource to be fed into the system so the system could produce more. Stan set his phone back on the table. He wasn’t finished yet.
Next, Stan opened Sophie’s TikTuk profile. She wasn’t live.

Earlier that evening, she had mentioned that she would be busy organizing new tenant agreements for Crown Jewel Tower. Fortunately, TikTuk’s gifting system wasn’t limited to livestreams. Users could also send premium gifts directly to posted videos, a feature that had grown increasingly popular among high-spending patrons who wanted to support creators without waiting for their next broadcast.
Those gifts still generated platform-wide notifications and counted toward a creator’s earnings.
He opened her profile. As always, Sophie’s content was polished and carefully curated.
A behind-the-scenes clip from her cheerleading appearance at the basketball game. A morning routine reel. A lifestyle video showcasing the panoramic view from her apartment in Crown Jewel Tower.
Each had already accumulated millions of views. Stan opened the cheerleading clip first.
He began sending premium video gifts, the platform’s highest-tier animated items, each leaving a twenty-four-hour visual effect over the video for future viewers.
Then he moved to the morning routine. Then the lifestyle post.
He continued down the page until all seven of her most recent uploads had received gifts, distributing approximately $1 billion across them with measured precision.
By tomorrow morning, the platform would be in an uproar.

The gift notifications alone would dominate TikTuk’s trending discussions, and Sophie would wake to a cascade of alerts informing her that Sir Streak had become the largest single video gifter in her account’s history by an almost incomprehensible margin.
Her favorability already stood at 125. The system responded immediately.
[Favorability tier: 120-129 (12× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $12 billion.]

chapters.title: Chapter 299: The Price Of Power
paragraphs: Anyways, Stan acknowledged the notification and switched to Maya’s profile. Just like Sophie, Maya was still new to the platform.

She had started streaming only a few weeks earlier, mostly to support promotional campaigns for her film projects. Her account contained only a handful of uploads; interview clips from the Ghost Signal press tour, behind-the-scenes footage from Unfinished Business, and a casual day-in-the-life reel she’d posted earlier that week.
Stan repeated the process.
He distributed another $1 billion in premium gifts across every recent upload, ensuring each video received a similar level of support.
Maya’s favorability had only recently crossed 120. The rebate arrived almost instantly.
[Favorability tier: 120-129 (12× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $12 billion.]
Stan leaned back in his chair.
Less than an hour earlier, he had transferred virtually every liquid dollar he possessed into Maya’s company. Now his cash balance had climbed past $100 billion.
The number felt almost detached from reality. A distant thought crossed his mind.

Banks and financial regulators were almost certainly seeing activity that would trigger every automated monitoring system they had. Transaction volumes of this magnitude would inevitably attract scrutiny, generating alerts, reviews, and perhaps entire teams of analysts trying to understand what they were looking at.
It wouldn’t matter. From the day the system had awakened, every rebate had appeared as an ordinary Internal Credit Adjustment. Even the bank he’s using can’t keep track of or spy on his account.

The funds arrived through transaction records that couldn’t be traced to any identifiable sender. No matching outgoing account. No corresponding institution. No audit trail leading back to a conventional source.
The pattern investigators would normally follow simply wasn’t there. Whether anyone attempted to investigate was irrelevant.
There was nothing for them to find. Stan dismissed the thought as quickly as it had appeared. He still had work to do.
Stan pulled up Xenia’s account next. She was live. A faint smile crossed his face.

Xenia had been one of his earliest bindings, back when he was still discovering the limits of the system. Over the weeks since then, her favorability had risen steadily, settling at around 90, placing her in the legacy 9× rebate tier, which System 2.0 had retained for targets whose favorability remained between 80 and 99.
He entered the stream as Sir Streak. The effect was immediate.
The moment his username appeared in the viewer list, the chat erupted.
@Epstein’s4thChild: "SIR STREAK!"
@604thOnBonnieBluesl’sLine: "THE KING IS HERE!"
@I’mAMinorForDrake: "HE ACTUALLY CAME!"
@Diddy’sEx: "XENIA, LOOK AT YOUR VIEWER LIST!"
Xenia had been live for nearly an hour, hosting a relaxed Q&A session for her audience about her fun experience with Star Entertainment...
Her stream manager noticed the username before she did.
Something flashed across the monitor beside the camera. Xenia looked over. Her eyes widened.
"...Sir Streak?
She leaned closer to the screen, almost as if she thought she’d misread it.
"Everyone..." she said, unable to hide the excitement in her voice. "Sir Streak is here."
The chat exploded all over again.
@JudebellinghamPleaseTouchMe: I was able to witness the Legendary Sir Streak in Action
@HeymenAndTheyArePigs: Guys, Guess How much he’ll spend this time around
@TheRock’sHairGel: I’m from another Stream, Sir Streak just spent billions of dollars on some random’s Stream before coming here
@KevinHartIsGay?: @TheRock’sHairGel I know he’s rich and all that but come on bro, come up with a better lie, who will spend billions on streams...
@TheRock’sHairGel: Iswr on my dick I’m not lying!
@KevinHartIsGay?: And you expect me to believe that?
@TheRock’sHairGel: Just go check bro, it’s not that hard...
@ToeSnifferSupreme: Its actually real! All Hail The Big Boss🙇
@KevinHartIsGay?: I don’t believe you two, I’m coming, lemme go check
Ignoring the comment section, Stan opened the gifting menu. Then, with practiced calm, he began sending gifts. Premium rockets. Golden crowns.
Mythic-tier animations that only the platform’s biggest spenders ever touched. One after another, they flooded the stream.
Meanwhile, @KevinHartIsGay? joined the stream again but was to shocked to type anything...
@ToeSnifferSupreme: @KevinHartIsGay? So what do you have to say doubting Thomas 😏
@TheRock’sHairGel: @KevinHartIsGay? Is to shocked to talk😂😭
@ToeSnifferSupreme: Don’t be shocked @KevinHartIsGay? It’s just chicken change to Sir Streak, if not, why else will he gift those so casually, that’s why he’s the G.O.A.T’ED Gifter...
@KevinHartIsGay?: Sigh
Meanwhile, Stan kept gifting, the animated effects stacked across the screen in an almost uninterrupted procession as the gift total climbed higher and higher.
By the time the broadcast ended an hour later, Stan had spent $5 billion.
Xenia had long since stopped trying to maintain the polished composure expected of an established streamer. She laughed. She teared up.
She repeatedly thanked Sir Streak, sometimes losing her train of thought halfway through her sentences as another wave of gifts appeared.
Near the end of the stream, she simply looked into the camera, smiled helplessly, and shook her head.
"I... I don’t even know what to say anymore."
She laughed softly, brushing away a tear. The fact she knew Stan just made this even more absurd. "Thank you, Sir Streak. Really... thank you."
The chat never calmed down.
Every new gift reignited another wave of excitement, and by the end of the broadcast, the stream had become one of the most talked-about events on the platform that evening.
The system chimed.
[Favorability tier: 90-99 (9× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $45 billion deposited into linked account.]
Stan glanced at the notification, closed the stream, and exited the app.
He sat quietly at the dining table, his phone resting face-down before him.
The apartment was silent. His liquid cash balance had just crossed $122 billion. Only a few hours earlier, it had been $620 million.
The difference wasn’t merely the result of a profitable evening. It was the consequence of finally using the system the way it had always been intended to be used.

Until tonight, the Supreme Rebate System had functioned almost passively. It had rewarded him generously for a handful of investments and purchases, but he had never truly treated it as the scalable engine it was.
System 2.0 had changed that.
With higher rebate tiers, more daily bindings, and additional weekly rebate cycles, the system was no longer just generating wealth.
It was compounding it. At this scale, the figures had begun to lose their intuitive meaning.
A hundred billion dollars wasn’t personal wealth in the ordinary sense.
It was the sort of capital managed by sovereign wealth funds, multinational investment firms, and central financial institutions.
Stan leaned back in his chair. His thoughts drifted briefly to the Introduction to Earth.
The book had cost one system point. One point was One billion dollars.
At his current balance, he could afford roughly 110 system points. He still had no idea what that actually meant.

The introductory book had been little more than a primer. What would a genuine cultivation manual cost? An advanced body-tempering pill? A spirit weapon? A storage artifact? What if he could get all these from the system, what will be their cost?
Whatever lay deeper in the catalog, it was almost certainly more valuable, and more expensive, than anything he had seen so far.
For the first time since acquiring the system, he possessed enough capital to explore those higher tiers without hesitation.
He reached out with a thought. The system shop unfolded before him.
The interface shimmered briefly before settling into place.
[Shop inventory refreshed.]
[New items available.]
The catalog expanded across his vision. Rows of unfamiliar entries scrolled into existence, each carrying a name, a price, and a promise of something far beyond the ordinary world.
Stan drew a slow, measured breath. Then he began to read.

Stan leaned back in his chair.
Less than an hour earlier, he had transferred virtually every liquid dollar he possessed into Maya’s company.
Now his cash balance had climbed past $100 billion.
The number felt almost detached from reality.
A distant thought crossed his mind.
Banks and financial regulators were almost certainly seeing activity that would trigger every automated monitoring system they had.
Transaction volumes of this magnitude would inevitably attract scrutiny, generating alerts, reviews, and perhaps entire teams of analysts trying to understand what they were looking at.
It wouldn’t matter.
From the day the system had awakened, every rebate had appeared as an ordinary Internal Credit Adjustment.
Even the bank he’s using can’t keep track of or spy on his account.
The funds arrived through transaction records that couldn’t be traced to any identifiable sender.
No matching outgoing account.
No corresponding institution.
No audit trail leading back to a conventional source.
The pattern investigators would normally follow simply wasn’t there.
Whether anyone attempted to investigate was irrelevant.
There was nothing for them to find.
Stan dismissed the thought as quickly as it had appeared.
He still had work to do.
Stan pulled up Xenia’s account next.
She was live.
A faint smile crossed his face.
Xenia had been one of his earliest bindings, back when he was still discovering the limits of the system.

Over the weeks since then, her favorability had risen steadily, settling at around 90, placing her in the legacy 9× rebate tier, which System 2.0 had retained for targets whose favorability remained between 80 and 99.
He entered the stream as Sir Streak.
The effect was immediate.
The moment his username appeared in the viewer list, the chat erupted.
@Epstein’s4thChild: "SIR STREAK!"
@604thOnBonnieBluesl’sLine: "THE KING IS HERE!"
@I’mAMinorForDrake: "HE ACTUALLY CAME!"
@Diddy’sEx: "XENIA, LOOK AT YOUR VIEWER LIST!"
Xenia had been live for nearly an hour, hosting a relaxed Q&A session for her audience about her fun experience with Star Entertainment...
Her stream manager noticed the username before she did.
Something flashed across the monitor beside the camera.
Xenia looked over.
Her eyes widened.
"...Sir Streak?
She leaned closer to the screen, almost as if she thought she’d misread it.
"Everyone..." she said, unable to hide the excitement in her voice.
"Sir Streak is here."
The chat exploded all over again.
@JudebellinghamPleaseTouchMe: I was able to witness the Legendary Sir Streak in Action
@HeymenAndTheyArePigs: Guys, Guess How much he’ll spend this time around
@TheRock’sHairGel: I’m from another Stream, Sir Streak just spent billions of dollars on some random’s Stream before coming here
@KevinHartIsGay?: @TheRock’sHairGel I know he’s rich and all that but come on bro, come up with a better lie, who will spend billions on streams...
@TheRock’sHairGel: Iswr on my dick I’m not lying!
@KevinHartIsGay?: And you expect me to believe that?
@TheRock’sHairGel: Just go check bro, it’s not that hard...
@ToeSnifferSupreme: Its actually real!
All Hail The Big Boss🙇
@KevinHartIsGay?: I don’t believe you two, I’m coming, lemme go check
Ignoring the comment section, Stan opened the gifting menu.
Then, with practiced calm, he began sending gifts.
Premium rockets.
Golden crowns.
Mythic-tier animations that only the platform’s biggest spenders ever touched.
One after another, they flooded the stream.
Meanwhile, @KevinHartIsGay? joined the stream again but was to shocked to type anything...
@ToeSnifferSupreme: @KevinHartIsGay?
So what do you have to say doubting Thomas 😏
@TheRock’sHairGel: @KevinHartIsGay?
Is to shocked to talk😂😭
@ToeSnifferSupreme: Don’t be shocked @KevinHartIsGay?
It’s just chicken change to Sir Streak, if not, why else will he gift those so casually, that’s why he’s the G.O.A.T’ED Gifter...
@KevinHartIsGay?: Sigh
Meanwhile, Stan kept gifting, the animated effects stacked across the screen in an almost uninterrupted procession as the gift total climbed higher and higher.
By the time the broadcast ended an hour later, Stan had spent $5 billion.
Xenia had long since stopped trying to maintain the polished composure expected of an established streamer.
She laughed.
She teared up.
She repeatedly thanked Sir Streak, sometimes losing her train of thought halfway through her sentences as another wave of gifts appeared.
Near the end of the stream, she simply looked into the camera, smiled helplessly, and shook her head.
I don’t even know what to say anymore."
She laughed softly, brushing away a tear.
The fact she knew Stan just made this even more absurd.
"Thank you, Sir Streak.
Really... thank you."
The chat never calmed down.
Every new gift reignited another wave of excitement, and by the end of the broadcast, the stream had become one of the most talked-about events on the platform that evening.
The system chimed.
[Favorability tier: 90-99 (9× rebate).]
[Rebate issued: $45 billion deposited into linked account.]
Stan glanced at the notification, closed the stream, and exited the app.
He sat quietly at the dining table, his phone resting face-down before him.
The apartment was silent.
His liquid cash balance had just crossed $122 billion.
Only a few hours earlier, it had been $620 million.
The difference wasn’t merely the result of a profitable evening.
It was the consequence of finally using the system the way it had always been intended to be used.
Until tonight, the Supreme Rebate System had functioned almost passively.
It had rewarded him generously for a handful of investments and purchases, but he had never truly treated it as the scalable engine it was.
System 2.0 had changed that.
With higher rebate tiers, more daily bindings, and additional weekly rebate cycles, the system was no longer just generating wealth.
It was compounding it.
At this scale, the figures had begun to lose their intuitive meaning.
A hundred billion dollars wasn’t personal wealth in the ordinary sense.
It was the sort of capital managed by sovereign wealth funds, multinational investment firms, and central financial institutions.
Stan leaned back in his chair.
His thoughts drifted briefly to the Introduction to Earth.
The book had cost one system point.
One point was One billion dollars.
At his current balance, he could afford roughly 110 system points.
He still had no idea what that actually meant.
The introductory book had been little more than a primer.
What would a genuine cultivation manual cost?
An advanced body-tempering pill?
A spirit weapon?
A storage artifact?
What if he could get all these from the system, what will be their cost?
Whatever lay deeper in the catalog, it was almost certainly more valuable, and more expensive, than anything he had seen so far.
For the first time since acquiring the system, he possessed enough capital to explore those higher tiers without hesitation.
He reached out with a thought.
The system shop unfolded before him.
The interface shimmered briefly before settling into place.
[Shop inventory refreshed.]
[New items available.]
The catalog expanded across his vision.
Rows of unfamiliar entries scrolled into existence, each carrying a name, a price, and a promise of something far beyond the ordinary world.
Stan drew a slow, measured breath.
Then he began to read.

chapters.title: Chapter 300: Beyond Imagination
paragraphs: Stan opened the system shop and waited as the interface loaded.

The catalog had refreshed. The clean, empty display he had glimpsed earlier had expanded into a far more extensive inventory, neatly organized into layered categories. Every item was accompanied by a brief description, a summary of its intended use, and a price listed in system points.
He started reading through the entries.
[SYSTEM SHOP]
[Cultivation Manuals]
The first category was, predictably, the largest.

The system had stocked an extensive collection of cultivation techniques drawn, if the descriptions were to be believed, from the libraries of ancient sects. The catalog was neatly organized according to traditional classifications, ranging from relatively common manuals to techniques of extraordinary rarity.
Stan scrolled through them with the careful attention of a man less interested in buying than in understanding the scope of what the system was offering.

The lower-tier manuals cost one or two system points. They bore names such as Iron Body Heart Sutra (a basic body-tempering technique), Five Elements Foundation Manual (an entry-level elemental cultivation primer), and Bright Lotus Breathing Method (a meditative qi-circulation framework). Each entry included a concise annotation detailing its era of origin, its grade within the old sect classification systems, and the estimated time a practitioner would typically require to achieve a meaningful cultivation breakthrough.

The mid-tier offerings ranged from three to six system points. Their names were considerably grander: Nine Yang Tempering Sutra, Heaven Splitting Sword Intent Manual, and Verdant Mountain Body-Forging Technique. Their descriptions promised dramatically greater power, though several carried warnings that improper comprehension could lead to serious cultivation deviations.
At the very top of the cultivation manual section sat a single entry priced at ten system points, the highest cost Stan had encountered anywhere in the shop.
He lingered on it.
[Heaven-Severing Primordial Origin Sutra]

A peak cultivation technique attributed to the founding patriarch of the lost Primordial Origin Sect. Said to encompass the unity of all elements, the cycle of creation and destruction, and the path from mortal flesh to Severed-Heaven Ascension. Practitioners who reach its higher realms are reputed to transcend the very constraints of the world. Comprehension requires Qi affinity beyond the mortal threshold.
[Cost: 10 System Points.]
Stan studied the description in silence.
The name alone sounded like a parody of every cultivation novel he had ever read.
’Heaven-Severing.’
’Primordial Origin.’
’Severed-Heaven Ascension.’
On the surface, it was exactly the sort of impossibly overpowered technique a novice web novelist might invent to give their protagonist an absurd advantage. Except this was not a novel.
This was the system’s shop, and in the weeks since its activation, it had given him no reason to question the authenticity of anything it presented.

If the ’Heaven-Severing Primordial Origin Sutra’ occupied the very pinnacle of the shop’s cultivation manuals, then it was almost certainly exactly what its name claimed to be: a supreme technique from an age when methods like this had truly existed.
He sighed and moved on to the next category.
[Tempering Techniques]

This section was much smaller, containing only six items priced between two and seven system points. Unlike the cultivation manuals, these were not complete cultivation systems but specialized refinement methods, techniques designed to strengthen specific aspects of the body between major cultivation breakthroughs.
’Nine-Forge Marrow Cleansing Technique.’
’Frostfire Sinew Tempering.’
’Stellar Bone Resonance Method.’
Each description promised dramatic improvements to the body, but every one of them came with the same prerequisite: a sufficient reserve of Qi to perform the tempering process.
Stan continued scrolling, entering the...
[Weapons section]
The weapons section caught his attention next.
The system offered an impressive arsenal of cold steel: swords, spears, daggers, sabers, halberds, and a variety of more exotic weapons, each bearing names that practically radiated lethality.
’Phoenix Cry Saber.’
’Riversong Twin Blades.’
’Silent Star Spear.’
Their descriptions promised extraordinary sharpness, nearly indestructible construction, and the ability to channel and amplify Qi-based weapon arts. Prices ranged from two to eight system points.
Stan lingered on the section for a moment before scrolling past.
The weapons were undeniably cool. The thirteen-year-old version of him would have been completely enthralled.
The current version was considerably more practical.

In a modern world dominated by firearms, ballistic armor, drones, precision-guided missiles, and countless other forms of advanced weaponry, what exactly was he supposed to do with a Phoenix Cry Saber? Walk into a gunfight carrying a sword?
The romance of cold steel had a habit of ending the moment someone pulled out a nine-millimeter handgun, never mind military-grade hardware.
There was an even more fundamental issue.
Like the cultivation manuals, every weapon relied on Qi to unlock its true capabilities.

He possessed Qi, a limited reserve left behind by the Bone-Tempering Pill and the Jade Purity Elixir, but there was no ambient Qi in the modern world. Ancient cultivators had replenished themselves by absorbing spiritual energy from their surroundings. He couldn’t.
Whatever Qi he currently possessed was all he had.
Using it to empower a weapon in a firefight would only drain a resource he had no reliable way of recovering.
With that thought, he moved on to the next category.
[Pills and Elixirs]
The consumables section was enormous.

Bone-Tempering Pills, Marrow-Cleansing Pills, Soul-Strengthening Pills, Qi Condensation Pills, Qi Replenishment Pills, healing elixirs, breakthrough catalysts, longevity tonics, an entire pharmacopoeia of medicinal treasures straight out of the cultivation novels he had spent years reading. Except now they were no longer fiction. They were items he could acquire at the appropriate cost.
Prices ranged from one to nine system points, with the more potent medicines clustered toward the upper end of the scale.
The Bone-Tempering Pill he had consumed earlier that day was listed at three system points.
The Jade Purity Elixir cost four.
Higher-grade variants of both were also available.
’Greater Bone-Tempering Pill.’
’Heavenly Jade Purity Elixir.’

They were priced at six and seven system points respectively, each accompanied by a note explaining that their effects scaled with the practitioner’s existing cultivation foundation rather than providing a fixed increase.
Stan committed the prices to memory before continuing through the catalog.
Then he saw it.
[Inventory Item]
The listing sat in a category of its own, tucked off to one side and priced at five system points.
[System Inventory, Personal Spatial Storage]

[A pocket dimension keyed to the user’s spiritual signature. Capacity equivalent to four standard football fields. Items stored within experience no decay, no temperature variation, and no environmental effects. Retrieval and deposit operate via mental command and require no Qi expenditure on the user’s part.] [Permanent acquisition.] [One-time cost: 5 system points.]
Stan stopped scrolling.
He read the description once. Then a second time. A pocket dimension.

The sort of spatial storage that had occupied countless pages of the cultivation novels he had devoured over the years. Storage rings. Spatial bags. Bottomless repositories that allowed people to carry entire libraries, armories, and fortunes without the slightest inconvenience.
He had seen the concept so often that it had become little more than a genre cliché.
The system was offering him one.

More importantly, the description explicitly stated that depositing and retrieving items required no Qi expenditure. The inventory functioned through the system’s own underlying mechanisms, drawing on whatever power source sustained the system itself.
He could use it freely, no matter how depleted his own Qi reserves became.
The implications were obvious.

He could carry the Introduction to Earth book without physically transporting it. The Bone-Tempering Pill. The Jade Purity Elixir. Future cultivation manuals. Weapons, if he ever decided to buy them. Cash. Valuables.
Anything that fit inside. All instantly accessible with a single thought.
For five system points.
He didn’t hesitate. Opening his banking app, he willed another conversion.
Five billion dollars vanished from his account in a clean, instantaneous transaction.
[System Points: +5]
He spent them immediately.
[Purchase confirmed.]
[System Inventory unlocked.]

A faint warmth blossomed behind his sternum, subtle enough that he almost missed it. It lingered for only a heartbeat before fading, leaving behind an inexplicable sense that something had attached itself to his very being.
His spatial storage.
Stan’s gaze drifted to the empty Jade Purity Elixir bottle still resting on the kitchen counter.
He focused on it.
Store.
The bottle vanished. Not faded nor dissolved. It simply ceased to exist in the physical world.
He instinctively checked his Qi reserve. It was unchanged. Not even the slightest fluctuation.
A smile tugged at the corner of his mouth.
Retrieve.
The bottle materialized in his palm with effortless immediacy. Cool glass settled naturally into his hand, as though it had never been anywhere else.
"It still feels surreal," he murmured to the empty kitchen. "Doing things like this so casually."
He repeated the process twice more.
Store!
Retrieve!!
Store!!!
Retrieve!!!
Each activation was flawless. Instantaneous. Effortless.
The system’s spatial storage worked exactly as advertised.
Satisfied, Stan set the bottle back on the counter and turned his attention to the second item that had caught his eye.
